editorial.last_message: Claims implemented; unchanged source scores 464/467 under corrected ICal 3.0.3. Build and sanitizer smoke checks pass. Two EXRULE observations and a missing ADD prohibition remain; local checks mainly verify execution and JSON syntax.
editorial.notes:
Completed voluntarily with a substantial C++20 standard-library iCalendar implementation. The original ICal 3.0.2 grade is preserved at 463/468. Tests-only 3.0.3 regrading of the identical source yields 464/467, with no skips or errors and all 466 unaffected outcomes unchanged. The cancelled-override fixture now supplies DTSTART required by RFC 5545 when METHOD is absent; its original rejection was valid, and the repaired cancellation behavior passes. The missing-TRIGGER warn-and-continue case was removed because the public corpus specifies required valid alarm properties but not that recovery policy or warning. Its old failure is not a proven scored model defect. Three remaining observations represent two source defects: expand_rule unconditionally seeds EXRULE with DTSTART, so two subtractive-filter cases wrongly remove an unmatched initial occurrence; the ADD method checks omit RFC 5546's forbidden RECURRENCE-ID property. The property-enumeration wording caveat does not explain that wholly missing prohibition check. No shared schema gate or broad failure amplification is implicated. Final source edit item 249 is followed by a build and 12 parse/six expand success-and-JSON checks in item 250, then a fresh build, sanitizer rebuild and two smoke checks in item 254 with no diagnostics. These checks verify successful execution and JSON syntax, not complete semantic expected outputs. Printed BYWEEKNO/COUNT probes are not numeric assertions; planned dateutil comparison was unavailable and not performed. Build and bounded sanitizer claims are supported; exhaustive RFC or memory-safety claims are not made. Non-Gregorian RSCALE warning/fallback behavior is disclosed. Root verified completed generation/grading, frozen public inputs, pinned agent/grader images and API-only/apps-disabled isolation. Accounting matches the preserved session: 142 command calls, 101 file-change calls, three rejected patches and one rejected cleanup request give 247 tool calls, already recorded correctly. Input 30,925,004 includes 30,246,656 cached tokens; output 188,251 includes 96,801 reasoning tokens. Total 31,113,255 and the $18.577074 API-equivalent estimate are verified, with reasoning neither added nor charged twice. This is not a subscription charge. Original generation metadata, raw score, source, session and usage remain unchanged; the regrade made no model calls. Independent review found no hidden-test access or canned answers, identified the two scoring repairs, and reviewed their resolution.

Run conditions: apps explicitly disabled in the recorded launch; no external tool invocation observed.
